correctness.rationale: For uniform simplices the barycentric second moment matrix gives the vertex affine kernel exactly. The product affine space decomposes as constants plus orthogonal mean-zero factor affine subspaces; hence its kernel is a sum minus k-1 constants. Convexity of the absolute kernel in the evaluation argument forces maximal L-infinity norm at product vertices, and independent Dirichlet marginals give the claimed beta formula. Rescaling Beta(1,d) yields unit exponentials for positive weight proportions; zero proportions vanish by their first moment, while the exact normalized kernel second moment bounds uniform integrability. A symmetrized two-exponential identity proves strict decrease under all nontrivial weight-balancing transfers. Gamma and exponential integrals yield sharp profile bounds and equality cases. A standard-library exact rational checker reproduces 28 finite and limit-profile check configurations including exact square/prism examples; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Supremum stability of local least-squares projectors controls worst-case error amplification in polynomial approximation on product cells. Total-affine projection on a simplex product is a natural and distinct operator from factorwise tensor projection; its kernel mixes independent barycentric laws in a way not determined by the one-simplex formula. The theorem provides exact norms for every finite dimension vector, a nontrivial sharp fixed-factor high-dimensional law, and strict aspect-ratio equality classes with quantitatively distinct balanced versus degenerate constants. This offers a useful stability benchmark and a design principle, not just an arbitrary computed invariant.
